comparison_scope: agentic JS deobfuscation and environment-rebuild skills
static JS decompiler and semantic-renaming tools
cross-domain reverse-engineering MCP systems used as workflow references

dimensions.label: Browser MCP portability
dimensions.market_signal: Advanced MCP reverse stacks expose CDP, network interception, runtime JS hooks, debugger control, and automation through different server APIs.
dimensions.target_behavior: Generate adapter-neutral MCP execution plans, record which server and tools actually ran, then ingest execution records into evidence artifacts.

dimensions.label: Anti-detection profile discipline
dimensions.market_signal: Modern browser reverse tooling increasingly includes anti-detection browsers, stealth contexts, fingerprint parity, storage-state profiles, preload hooks, and profile switching.
dimensions.target_behavior: Choose named anti-detection profiles, record the profile in the bundle, and separate bypass evidence from signer or replay correctness.

dimensions.label: Task decomposition lanes
dimensions.market_signal: Strong skill packs split AST deobfuscation, environment patching, crypto entry discovery, runtime capture, and delivery into reusable lanes with clear next actions.
dimensions.target_behavior: Keep one primary router, but expose explicit sub-lanes and next-action recommendations so the operator can deepen one path without losing the global workflow.

dimensions.label: Evidence state machine
dimensions.market_signal: Best-in-class workflows distinguish planned actions, observed runtime facts, inferred static hypotheses, accepted server behavior, and replay parity.
dimensions.target_behavior: Never collapse planned, executed, observed, inferred, runtime-accepted, and replay-verified states.

dimensions.label: Runtime capture breadth
dimensions.market_signal: Advanced browser tooling captures request initiators, fetch/XHR bodies, cookie and storage writes, headers, call frames, crypto helpers, workers, and wasm hints.
dimensions.target_behavior: Prefer minimal hooks first, then widen capture surfaces only when the blocker requires it.

dimensions.label: Static toolchain integration
dimensions.market_signal: Leading static paths prioritize source-map recovery, then combine bundle splitting, obfuscator cleanup, AST transforms, semantic naming, and version diffing.
dimensions.target_behavior: Use source-map and specialist tools to reduce reading cost, but verify recovered logic against browser evidence or replay.

dimensions.label: Environment rebuild loop
dimensions.market_signal: Practical reverse workflows advance through first-divergence logs and smallest-causal-unit environment patches instead of broad window/document shims.
dimensions.target_behavior: Drive local rebuild from observed divergence and preserve every patch as an auditable artifact.

dimensions.label: Delivery and replay quality
dimensions.market_signal: The strongest workflows produce reusable Node/Python/proxy handoff artifacts from accepted evidence and classify divergent or rejected replay records into repair lanes.
dimensions.target_behavior: Only call delivery ready when replay or server acceptance supports it, generate replay clients from accepted records, and keep unresolved signers parameterized.

dimensions.label: Domain boundary handoffs
dimensions.market_signal: Advanced RE ecosystems span JS, WASM, packets, Android, native binaries, and debugger MCPs, but each lane needs a concrete artifact boundary and a validated handoff record.
dimensions.target_behavior: Hand off to packet, mobile, WASM, or binary analysis only after preserving and validating a specific boundary artifact.

dimensions.label: Release data safety
dimensions.market_signal: Public reverse-engineering packages are high leak-risk because captures, HARs, PCAPs, cookies, tokens, and local paths are easy to commit accidentally.
dimensions.target_behavior: Gate every public export with tracked-file, secret, path, fixture, and generated-artifact checks.
